label:
Casein for
fining wine
note: Milk protein fining agents may need to be declared as allergens; Australia and New Zealand require declaration of fining agents that may be allergenic (Wikipedia); the EU rule was not opened.

about.text: A milk protein used to clean up white wine: it binds the polyphenols that make wine brown and bitter, clumps, and sinks. It is racked off with the lees, so little or none should remain.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.

how.text: Fining also runs the other way: protein fining agents tame tannin in red wine.

facts.v: Browning-prone polyphenols such as leucoanthocyanins; lowers colour, browning potential and turbidity
Lowered polymeric flavanols; casein also lowered monomeric and oligomeric ones
Allergen worries and EU rules push non-allergenic agents; in one Douro study only potassium caseinate and PVPP cut colour significantly
